To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the interaction between funding and market liquidity is different during different crises.
the subprime financial and the European sovereign debt crises were caused by different factors, but both crises had similar consequences.

(a) funding liquidity shocks cause declines in market liquidity, (b) funding liquidity shocks have a stronger impact on market liquidity during the European sovereign crisis than the subprime crisis, (c) funding liquidity is more fragile during the European sovereign than the subprime financial crises, and (d) the fragility of market liquidity is higher during the European sovereign financial crisis than the subprimes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction between funding and market liquidity and their effects on asset returns.
a question of which cause is more important in financial market liquidity during a financial crisis.
the question of whether the decline in market liquidity is a cause of the decline in funding liquidity or the other way around.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the subprime crisis was mainly caused by funding liquidity shocks, and the European sovereign debt was caused by the simultaneous shocks to both market and funding liquidity.
the interaction of market liquidity and funding liquidity is not always a vicious circle. It can be a virtuous circle as well.
the malfunction in the interbank funding market is the primary reason for the reduction of market liquidity during financial crises.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the subprime crisis was caused by the malfunction of the interbank market, while the European crisis was caused by a combination of the malfunction of the funding and the market liquidity.
the interaction between funding and market liquidites is a two-way relationship, and that the interaction is asymmetric between funding and market liquidity.
the interaction between funding and market liquidity is not always the same, but is affected by the nature of the crisis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the interaction between funding and market liquidity should not be ignored when we study liquidity in financial markets.
the malfunction in the interbank funding market is a key driver of market illiquidity.
the interaction between funding and market liquidity is a two-way street: funding liquidity affects market liquidity, but market liquidity also affects funding liquidity.
